Ornamentation

Dunmore Lasses

This is a great tune the way Matt Molloy plays it. Bflat flute with only a couple of rolls for ornamentation, as previously stated. I play along with my Olwell Bflat while cranking the disc. Credit should also be given to Moloney for such a great arrangement of this reel.
This is a great tune.

↳ Posted by Bazza on October 27th, 2020.

The Dunmore Lasses, X:8

I guess most people play c naturals, but that puts the tune in minor instead of dorian, which is pretty rare in Irish music. I found a few versions that avoid the c entirely, making it hexatonic. Here’s one way of doing it without attempting to transcribe any particular recording. Banjo Joe’s setting replaces the c in bars 1 and 4 of the B part with low As, but two recordings I found, including the Mulcahy Family, use a high e instead. The easiest way to avoid the c in the last bar of each line is to hold the A longer. Another option is to play AdbA instead of AcbA.
